standard.title: Pose questions
standard.description: pose questions about familiar objects, people, places and events
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have natural question-asking capacity from lived experience. No formal prior HASS inquiry skills curriculum.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students pose questions about familiar objects, people, places and events to guide their own inquiry.

nodes.label: Noticing and wondering
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify something they notice or are curious about when exploring a source (object, photograph, place, story) and express it as a question.
nodes.minimum_width: Generate at least one question about a provided source using a prompted stem (What is...? Where is...? Why does...?).
nodes.typical_width: Generate multiple questions about familiar objects, people, places and events after being prompted to observe carefully; use a range of question stems (What, Where, Who, Why, How).
wider: Generate questions before and after an excursion or visiting community member, comparing what they wanted to know with what they found out
Sort questions by type (What/Where/Who questions vs Why/How questions) and discuss which are easier to answer and why
nodes.hinge_reason: If students cannot generate their own questions from observation, all subsequent inquiry work is teacher-driven rather than student-initiated — the questioning habit is the foundation of the entire inquiry skills strand.

response_modes.reason: At Foundation, question generation is a new habit. Build a class repertoire of question stems displayed visually, and practise generating questions from multiple different sources before expecting independence.

success_criteria: Generates at least one question about a provided source using a question stem
Question relates to something observable or inferable from the source

nodes.label: Posing inquiry questions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can pose questions that would guide an investigation about a familiar object, person, place or event, distinguishing between questions they can answer from memory and those that need investigation.
nodes.minimum_width: Pose at least one question about a familiar topic that requires seeking information beyond personal memory.
nodes.typical_width: Pose questions about family and places that would guide an inquiry; identify which questions can be answered from personal experience and which require investigation from sources.
wider: Develop questions about what makes events and places special, generating both factual and personal-response questions
Pose questions for a family member or familiar adult and explain why that person would be a good source

response_modes.reason: This node integrates noticing from Node 1 with directing inquiry — questions now have an investigative purpose, not just curiosity expression.

success_criteria: Poses at least one question that would require finding information from a source
Can identify whether a question can be answered from memory or needs investigation
